main_issue: Whether to keep the leaver's chosen Korean BBQ lunch or switch to another restaurant (given D's vegetarian day), and how to choose the new place (Japanese vs asking the leaver).

A-B.evidence: B questions changing the place (8,10,13) and asks to consult her (26); A refuses: 'We need to move on' (14), 'let's not bother her with it' (29).

A-C.evidence: C wants a quick decision (19,23,27); A agrees 'He's right, we need to decide' (25) and 'Japanese works for everyone. I'll book it' (29).

A-D.evidence: A accepts D's need to change place (7), then adopts D's suggestions Chinese/Italian (17) and Japanese (21); D says 'we need to find another place' (6) and proposes Japanese (20).

B-C.evidence: B wants to think about her preferences and ask her (22,26); C replies 'That will just take more time' (27) and pushes to pick Japanese.

B-D.evidence: B asks if it could work (10) while D says no (6); D then says 'Agent B has a point' (20) but proposes Japanese, which B questions (22).

C-D.evidence: C accepts either Chinese or Italian (19), then endorses D's Japanese suggestion: 'Japanese is quick and has options for everyone' (23, 27).
